text:
Climate technology firm Aether Fuels has successfully constructed, commissioned, and operated its integrated sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) technology platform at its Chicago, Illinois research and development (R&D) facility.

The demonstration line combines the company’s 2.5 barrel-per-day (bpd) Aurora tri-converter and upgrader units, integrated together with North Carolina technology development firm RTI’s existing Fischer-Tropsch reactor in a key step towards scale-up and commercial validation.

It used Kentucky landfill-derived renewable natural gas (RNG) and industrial captured carbon dioxide (CO2) feedstocks in an electrified syngas generation process to produce SAF meeting ASTM D7566 specification. The production was certified by third-party AmSpec.

Aether Fuels believes it is the first company in North America to produce SAF from mass-balanced RNG and captured industrial CO2 at scale, in line with ASTM standards.

Under the ASTM D7566 specification, alternative fuels can be blended with conventional kerosene up to 50% without requiring modification to existing aircraft tanks, pipelines, or airport fueling systems.

Conor Madigan, CEO and co-founder of Aether Fuels, said the company started with a pilot demonstration, then scaled up over 50 times in standalone demo units, before bringing together the demo units in an integrated line to produce ASTM-standard SAF.

Dhaval Shah, Chief Technology Officer at Aether Fuels, added, “The data from this demonstration informs and de-risks the design of our 50-bpd Project Beacon plant in Singapore, as we continue our rapid journey to large-scale commercial deployment.”

In May, Aether Fuels announced it was partnering with Singapore-based FlyORO Technologies to explore the development of a SAF supply chain, centred on Project Beacon.

Project Beacon is Aether’s planned commercial demonstration facility at the Aster Pulau Bukom refinery in Singapore, which aims to be the first commercial-scale SAF facility in Southeast Asia and will use a more feedstock-flexible route to production using waste carbon.

India's overall Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) readiness is estimated to be around 52 per cent, indicating moderate but advancing readiness as the country moves from early-stage development towards wider SAF adoption, a report said on Tuesday.

The joint report by US aircraft major Boeing and Roundtable on Sustainable Biomaterials (RSB) also shows that India's opportunity will depend not only on production potential, but on the coordinated development of the wider enabling ecosystem.

India has set blending targets of 1 per cent by 2027, 2 per cent by 2028 and eventually 5 per cent by 2030.

The country is also committed to participating in the International Civil Aviation Organization's Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) from 2027.

Under a 5 per cent blending scenario in 2030, SAF demand covering both domestic and international aviation is projected at approximately 720 million litres (about 0.6 million tonnes per year), compared with an estimated production potential of 14-33 million tonnes per year, as per the report.

The report carries out a comprehensive assessment of India's readiness for SAF adoption, providing an evidence-based roadmap for the country's next phase of SAF development.

"The report finds India's overall SAF readiness to be 52 per cent, indicating moderate but advancing readiness as the country moves from early-stage development toward wider SAF adoption," it said.

The report examines and uncovers strengths and opportunities in India's SAF adoption journey, as aviation demand continues to grow. It has been developed by RSB using a methodology which evaluates India's preparedness across nine dimensions – feedstock, production capacity, policy and regulation, supply chains and logistics, market demand, investment and financing, research and development, technology readiness, and enabling infrastructure and services.

"As one of the world's fastest-growing aviation markets, India has an important role in enabling sustainable aviation and pursuing a deliberate and well-researched path to SAF adoption is key," said Salil Gupte, president, Boeing India and South Asia.

"This report is valuable because it confirms exactly where India has the foundational capacity to enable SAF adoption and because it identifies specific opportunities ahead," Gupte added.

Aligned with the industry, the report stated, Boeing is committed to supporting airline customers and policymakers in India and globally in achieving their emissions reduction goals by helping to build a robust SAF ecosystem.

"India's Sustainable Aviation Fuel opportunity is substantial. This assessment gives stakeholders a common evidence base from which to act, and RSB looks forward to continuing to convene and support the collaboration needed to translate India's potential into sustainable impact," said RSB's Executive Director, Bettina Paschke.

Coordinated action and collaboration across government, industry, financiers, and other stakeholders will be important to support the development of the SAF market in India, it stated.

text:
PTI

Updated On Sep 30, 2026 at 09:30 AM IST

Jet fuel demand in India would rise from about 192,000 barrels per day in 2024 to 277,000 barrels per day by 2031, providing a strong market for the Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), as per a report released on Monday.

The government has announced SAF blending roadmap starting with 1 per cent blending in 2027 and increasing to 2 per cent in 2028 and 5 per cent in 2030 to decarbonise the aviation industry.

Advt

The report jointly developed by S&P Global Energy and the SAF Association estimates that the SAF demand will be 46,000 tonne in 2027, which would rise to 250,000 tonne in 2030.

India's aviation sector is expected to remain one of the fastest-growing sources of refined product demand through 2060, providing a strong foundation for developing a domestic SAF market, the report said.

"This expansion is driven by rising middle-class mobility, continued growth in domestic and international air travel, airport infrastructure development, and ongoing airline fleet additions," it said.

The report, released at 2nd India SAF Conclave, noted that while some short-term weakness emerged in 2026, particularly in the international segment, the underlying demand trajectory remains firmly positive.

Advt

India's aviation fuel consumption softened in mid-2026, with July demand falling to about 180,000 barrel per day reflecting weaker flight activity, higher operating costs, and supply-side disruptions, it said.

However, first-half 2026 jet fuel consumption still increased by nearly 2 per cent year-over-year, suggesting the recent slowdown is temporary rather than structural and does not alter the longer-term growth outlook, the report said.

"The demand outlook is further supported by rising passenger traffic, the continued expansion of low-cost aviation, and increasing international connectivity," it said.

New infrastructure, including Navi Mumbai International Airport and Jewar Airport in Noida, is expected to ease capacity constraints and support additional growth in flight activity.

International aviation is likely to remain an important demand driver, with international seat capacity expanding faster than domestic capacity in 2026 despite higher ticket costs.

"Policy support is also expected to play an important role in sustaining aviation growth. A key structural driver is the government's continued focus on expanding air connectivity through UDAN (Ude Desh Ka Aam Nagrik) Regional Connectivity Scheme," the report said.

It highlighted that the government has introduced an aviation turbine fuel (ATF) pricing stabilization mechanism, including a fixed ATF price in Delhi and a dedicated stabilization fund.

While not a direct subsidy, the mechanism reduces fuel price volatility and improves cost visibility for airlines, it added.

description:
Today the first A350F aircraft – MSN700 – took to the skies for the very first time.

After the flight, Laurent Bussiere, lead flight test engineer enthused: “We are now starting the flight test campaign and we're all very proud to be part of today’s mission.
For all of us it’s a real milestone to be part of the first flight crew of a new aircraft.
text:
Today the first A350F aircraft – MSN700 – took to the skies for the very first time. This flight marked the beginning of the planned 10 month / 400 flight hour test campaign which will culminate in EASA Type Certification – paving the way to first customer deliveries of the world’s most efficient widebody freighter. As a new member of the A350 Family, A350F will deliver up to 40% lower fuel burn and CO₂ emissions compared with previous-generation freighters.

The crew of five on board were: Experimental Test Pilots Bernardo Saez-Benito Hernandez and Sylvain Guiraud; Test-Flight Engineer (TFE) Ludovic Girard; and Flight-Test-Engineers (FTEs) Laurent Bussiere and Jaime Angoloti Benavides.

Over the coming months, many more of Airbus’ flight test professionals will take part in the global certification flight test campaign – which feature two the complementary test aircraft:

MSN700 will focus on handling qualities, autopilot systems and performance. This aircraft has been equipped with a specialised tail skid and bumper to protect the structure (from a potential contact with the runway) during the take-off performance tests.

MSN701, meanwhile, will focus on system-related testing, including air conditioning, water & waste and comprehensive smoke detection testing. MSN701 will also perform the hot and cold weather campaign as well as visiting customers.

As of today, MSN701 has completed final assembly and is undergoing ground tests before entering the paintshop.

Celebrating a collective engineering excellence

Julien Puyou, Airbus’ Head of Widebody Programme comments: “From a bold vision on paper in 2021 to seeing the A350F fly for the first time today, this milestone is a triumph of pioneering spirit and collective determination.”

He adds: “Looking back at where we started when we launched the A350F programme, turning a revolutionary composite freighter design into physical reality has been an extraordinary human and industrial journey. Seeing our teams across Europe and beyond deliver breakthrough engineering – from delivering the largest main-deck cargo door in commercial aviation, conducting detailed large demonstrator testing, FAL final assembly, flight test instrumentation installation, ground testing, virtual development simulations and now the first flight in Toulouse – demonstrates what we can achieve when we unite around a shared goal."

What took place in the first flight?

The crew flew the aircraft for 4 hours and 10 minutes, during which they explored the aircraft’s handling characteristics in direct law, the engines’ behaviour, and core mechanical systems. The aircraft reached an indicated airspeed (IAS) of 340 kts and an altitude of 25,000 ft.

Validating control laws against predictive models

The main objective of the initial flight is to validate and clear the aircraft's control laws by comparing real-time flight performance against the pre-flight predictive models that established the handling qualities. To this end, the crew took off in direct law which provides direct manual control.

They progressively climbed to 10,000ft then to 25,000 ft to evaluate the aircraft’s behaviour and confirmed that the aircraft’s actual aerodynamics and structural model matched the models which the crew had previously flown in the simulator. Once this had been achieved, and everything was within acceptable thresholds, normal law was activated, in order to clear the flying aircraft with its full flight envelope protections, and across the normal speed range.

Validating primary systems in flight

Aside from confirming the aerodynamic and structural characteristics, the crew also evaluated the primary systems such as pressurisation (measuring potential leakage rates against ground baseline tests), communication, and navigation to ensure they functioned as expected, thus paving the way to launching the broader flight test campaign in subsequent flights.

Real-time telemetry and the Flight Test Instrumentation (FTI) suite

Key to the aircraft's role as a flight-test vehicle is its Flight Test Instrumentation (FTI) suite – developed by Airbus’ own Electrical Centre in Toulouse and integrated into the fuselage sections in Airbus Atlantic in Montoir-de-Bretagne and Airbus Aerostructures in Hamburg. During a flight test the FTI tracks thousands of parameters on-board and conveys telemetry to monitoring teams on the ground in real time.

After the flight, Laurent Bussiere, lead flight test engineer enthused: “We are now starting the flight test campaign and we're all very proud to be part of today’s mission. For all of us it’s a real milestone to be part of the first flight crew of a new aircraft. This aircraft is exceptional – its payload capabilities, fuel efficiency and flexibility show that it really will be a top freighter aircraft for all the airlines who will operate it.”
